anna_ml: Hey all — trying to bring up hf/my-new-chat and seeing a token-count regression vs the HF reference. Short repro: when input contains a non-breaking space (NBSP, U+00A0) tokenization differs between the HF tokenizer artifacts and Redwood's converted tokenizer. Anyone seen NBSP <-> normal-space normalization causing weird byte-fallback splits?

ben_infra: Hmm, can you paste the minimal repro and the two token lists?

anna_ml: Sure — small example below. HF tokenizer (from transformers) vs Redwood runtime tokenization after our conversion script.

anna_ml: ```python
from transformers import AutoTokenizer
# HF original
t = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained('hf/my-new-chat')
inp = 'Hello\u00A0world'  # NBSP between words
print('HF tokens:', t.tokenize(inp))
print('HF ids:', t(inp)['input_ids'])
# Converted-tokenizer run (local shim)
# converted = RedwoodTokenizer.from_config('./redwood_tokenizer')
# print('RW tokens:', converted.tokenize(inp))
```

anna_ml: HF tokens: ['Hello', '\u2581world']  (counts: 2)
anna_ml: Redwood (converted) tokens: ['Hello', '\\xc2', '\\xa0', 'world']  (counts: 4)

dave_research: Oof. That looks like the HF tokenizer pre-normalizer is running NFKC/NFC and then using a metachar/bytefallback that treats NBSP as a whitespace-like grapheme (merged into underline token \u2581 in some tokenizers). Our conversion likely left a different pretokenizer (byte-level fallback) enabled so NBSP is being encoded as raw bytes (\\xc2\\xa0).

ben_infra: Two axes to check: 1) the normalizer configured in the HF tokenizer (NFKC vs NFD vs none), 2) the pre_tokenizer (byte_fallback vs whitespace + byte_fallback). If HF's repo tokenizer had a custom normalizer mapping NBSP->SPACE, then our converter needs to replicate it.

anna_ml: Right — I dug into the HF tokenizer config.json and found no explicit normalizer entry — it defaults to "NFKC" for that model's tokenizer logic. Our conversion pipeline currently only copies the merges/vocab and enables byte_fallback pretokenizer by default.

eva_docs: We should capture this in onboarding checklist: "verify whitespace-equivalence (NBSP, ZWSP, NO-BREAK SPACE) between HF and Redwood pretokenizers" and add a unit test with the three examples.

ben_infra: Quick hack test: force the converted tokenizer to run a Normalizer step before byte fallback. In fast-tokenizers config it's something like:

ben_infra: ```json
{"normalizer": {"type": "nfkc"}, "pre_tokenizer": {"type": "byte_fallback"}}
```

ben_infra: After adding that, converted tokenize(inp) returns ['Hello', '\u2581world'] which matches HF.

dave_research: Nice. Two follow-ups: 1) add a small fuzz test in the conversion harness to enum all whitespace-like codepoints (NBSP, ZWSP, U+2007, regular space) and check tokenization parity, 2) log a tech-debt item to audit other normalizer flags (compatibility decomposition NFKD vs composition NFC can shift multi-codepoint graphemes).

anna_ml: I ran a quick quantization benchmark too — the additional normalizer step doesn't materially change tokenization latency (microseconds) but fixes a ton of eval regressions where reference metrics expected fewer tokens.

ci-bot: Regression run attached: https://ci.redwood.internal/runs/48592 — shows eval delta > 0.02 BLEU on chat-turn samples when NBSPs are present.

eva_docs: I'll update the onboarding doc and conversion README to call out this exact example and include the config snippet. Also will add a short note on special_tokens_map edge cases (e.g., if your HF tokenizer treated NBSP as part of a special token).

ben_infra: Action: I'll change the converter to copy normalizer settings and add a parity test for NBSP/ZWSP/regular-space. Assigning to @ben_infra. ETA EOD tomorrow.

anna_ml: Thanks — will re-run the model bring-up after the fix and post results. :thumbsup:

ben_infra: cc @dave_research for the audit item.

dave_research: ack. I'll scope the audit and put an RFC on the backlog.
